panduan.title: User Guide
panduan.hero_desc: A summary of the app's features — from signing in, managing OLTs, ONU registration, monitoring & alarms, map & ODP, to settings. Use the table of contents to jump to the part you need.
panduan.footer_before: Need more technical detail? Developer docs live in
panduan.footer_after: . For direct help, contact your system admin.
panduan.pengantar_intro: An FTTH (GPON/EPON) network management system for monitoring OLTs and ONUs and registering new ONUs from a single web dashboard — a SmartOLT/NetNumen alternative for ISPs.
panduan.pengantar_i0: ZTE (C300/C320/C600), C-Data (EPON/GPON), and HiOSO (EPON HA7304/HA7302) managed side by side. Feature coverage differs per vendor — ZTE C300/C320 is the most complete.
panduan.pengantar_i1: scheduled SNMP polling (every 5 minutes by default) collects PON port status, ONU online/offline, and RX levels; alarms are sent automatically to Telegram & the Android app.
panduan.pengantar_i2: register new ONUs (ZTE), configure WAN, VLAN, and TR069, plus reboot, rename, enable/disable, and delete ONUs — straight from the web.
panduan.pengantar_tip: The full user guide (PDF) is in the repository's docs/panduan folder.
panduan.peran_intro: Sign in with the email & password your admin created for you — there is no self-registration. You can change your password yourself on the Profile page. Once signed in, the menus and buttons you see depend on your account's role.
panduan.peran_i0: full access: manage OLTs, users, system settings, audit logs, and every ONU action — including disabling/enabling PON ports.
panduan.peran_i1: day-to-day operations on the OLTs they may access: monitoring, ONU registration & actions, map, and ODP. Cannot open Users, Settings, or Audit Logs, and cannot disable PON ports.
panduan.peran_i2: sees only the OLTs assigned to them plus the OLTs they added themselves (private OLTs, hidden from admins/operators), plus their own Telegram bot.
panduan.peran_i3: showcase account: sees sample data only; every write action (registration, reboot, delete, etc.) is rejected.
panduan.navigasi_intro: The left sidebar is the main menu. The top bar holds search, the language picker, the notification bell, and the account menu.
panduan.navigasi_i0: menus are grouped into Overview, OLT network, Field, Monitoring, Administration, and Help. Click the arrow icon to collapse/expand; on mobile, tap the menu icon to open it.
panduan.navigasi_i1: type an OLT name/IP or an ONU serial, customer name, interface, or MAC (at least 2 characters) to jump straight to it; ONU results open the port page with that row highlighted.
panduan.navigasi_i2: shows the latest alarms; the red number = unread active alarms. Click a notification to jump straight to the affected ONU/port/OLT; the check icon marks it read, or use Mark all as read.
panduan.navigasi_i3: open Profile (change your name, email, and password), pick Appearance (Dark, Light, or Follow System), and Log out. The language chosen in the language picker is saved to your account.
panduan.dashboard_intro: The first page after login: an overall summary of network health.
panduan.dashboard_i0: Stat cards: Total OLTs, Total ONUs, ONUs Online, and Active Alarms.
panduan.dashboard_i1: Polling trend chart, ONU status, OLT inventory, latest alarms, provisioning jobs, and a Remote ONU Actions card (Reboot, Enable, Disable without opening the port page).
panduan.dashboard_i2: Numbers come from the latest polling results and follow your OLT scope — they reflect the last few minutes, not second-by-second real time.
panduan.olt_intro: The SmartOLT menu lists OLTs in per-vendor tabs (ZTE, C-Data, HiOSO). Add one via the Add OLT button.
panduan.olt_i0: name, IP, SNMP v1/v2c (read community required; the write community is needed for ZTE C300/C320 ONU rename & enable/disable and HiOSO HA7302 ONU rename), and Telnet CLI credentials for every write action. SNMP v3 and SSH are not supported yet.
panduan.olt_i1: click to verify the OLT is reachable — it shows system info and detects the vendor/model (run it once after adding a ZTE C600).
panduan.olt_i2: so the OLT joins scheduled monitoring (ONU status & RX are refreshed periodically by the poller engine).
panduan.olt_i3: the On/Off button in the OLT list controls whether this OLT's alarm notifications are sent (evaluation still runs & is recorded) — handy during scheduled maintenance.
panduan.olt_i4: the Save icon on the OLT row writes the running config to the OLT's memory. Many NMS actions do not save automatically, so run it after registrations or config changes.
panduan.olt_tip: Secret fields (write community, CLI password) can be left blank while editing to keep the old values — no need to retype them.
panduan.port-onu_intro: From an OLT's detail page, open a PON port to see the ONUs beneath it with their status and RX levels. Links from alarms, notifications, and search highlight the target ONU row straight away.
panduan.port-onu_i0: online/offline, last down cause (LOS, power off/dying gasp), and interface.
panduan.port-onu_i1: signal-quality indicator; values outside the healthy range are flagged as warnings.
panduan.port-onu_i2: the refresh button performs a live SNMP read for that port/OLT (rate-limited to avoid stressing the OLT).
panduan.port-onu_i3: the Add port label pencil icon in the header stores a label in the NMS (not written to the OLT), also shown in the Android app; ZTE ports use the port description on the OLT.
panduan.port-pon_intro: Click a port on the chassis image in a ZTE OLT's detail page to open Port Detail: status, optics/SFP, and traffic — the Refresh from OLT button reads them live over CLI.
panduan.port-pon_i0: edit the PON port description (max 64 characters) and add tagged VLANs on uplink ports — both are saved (write) to the OLT immediately.
panduan.port-pon_i1: the button in the GPON Port Detail header (C300/C320; not yet on C600) cuts off or reconnects every ONU on that port (shutdown / no shutdown). The confirmation dialog states how many ONUs are affected.
panduan.port-pon_i2: only admins, or the partner who owns the private OLT — operators cannot. Every action is recorded in the Audit Logs.
panduan.port-pon_i3: one notification when the port is disabled and one when it is enabled again. While the port is down, port, ONU, and ODP alarms on it are held, and the port page shows a yellow banner.
panduan.port-pon_tip: Disabling/enabling a port does not save the config automatically, so the port comes back up if the OLT reboots. Enable the port first before Save Config, editing a port description, or adding an uplink VLAN — otherwise the disabled state is saved permanently.
panduan.cdata-vlan_intro: On C-Data OLTs running V3 firmware (GPON and EPON), the VLAN button in OLT Detail and clicking a port on the Front Panel read data live over Telnet CLI.
panduan.cdata-vlan_i0: view the VLAN list, then create a new VLAN (1–4094) and tag it on several uplink/PON ports at once.
panduan.cdata-vlan_i1: on GPON, PON ports join every new VLAN automatically — just tag the uplink. On EPON, PON ports run in Hybrid mode and must be ticked manually.
panduan.cdata-vlan_i2: status, optics (DDM), traffic, tagged/untagged VLANs, and a Tag VLAN field for Trunk/Hybrid ports.
panduan.cdata-vlan_i3: the NMS does not save automatically — press Save Config to make it permanent. Writing is limited to admins/operators or the partner who owns the OLT, and is recorded in the Audit Logs.
panduan.unconfigured_intro: The Unconfigured menu collects ONUs detected by a ZTE OLT but not yet registered — new-customer candidates.
panduan.unconfigured_i0: Pick an OLT and click Refresh Discovery; the First Seen column and the New badge (under 24 hours) help spot freshly installed ONUs.
panduan.unconfigured_i1: Click Register ONU to open the registration form with the serial pre-filled, or Bind to an existing ONU to replace a broken ONU (see the Bind ONU section).
panduan.provisioning_intro: Registering a new ONU on a ZTE OLT: fill in its identity, pick profiles, define the WAN service, then run the generated CLI script. The C600 uses the TR069 model (internet + management services, automatic management IP).
panduan.provisioning_i0: serial, slot/port, ONU ID (suggested automatically), and customer name. The Description field is separate from the name (optional, max 80 characters); left empty, the NMS fills it automatically as the hint under the field explains.
panduan.provisioning_i1: ONU type, T-CONT, and VLAN/IP profiles (synced per-OLT from the OLT).
panduan.provisioning_i2: PPPoE (user/pass), DHCP, static IP, or Bridge; add TR069 and Remote ONT as needed. The C600 does not support PPPoE/DHCP/static WAN.
panduan.provisioning_i3: pick the ODP this customer hangs off — the dropdown is filtered to the chosen slot/port, and the link is only created once the registration succeeds.
panduan.provisioning_i4: the CLI script updates automatically as you edit — review it before executing, or choose Generate script only to save it without touching the OLT.
panduan.provisioning_i5: the script runs on the OLT via Telnet; the result is recorded in the Registration History.
panduan.provisioning_tip: Every registration is recorded in the Registration History. C300/C320 scripts do not save automatically — run Save Config after a batch of registrations; C600 scripts already end with write.
panduan.bind-onu_intro: Swaps an old ONU's serial for a new ONU in the same slot, so the customer's configuration (VLAN, PPPoE, ODP, map pin) carries over without re-registering. ZTE C300/C320 only.
panduan.bind-onu_i0: Install the replacement ONU on the customer's line, open Unconfigured, then click Refresh Discovery.
panduan.bind-onu_i1: On the new ONU's row, click Bind to an existing ONU, then pick the old ONU from the same port (ONUs that are down are listed first).
panduan.bind-onu_i2: Read the warnings: only the SN changes — WiFi/web settings on the old ONU do not carry over, and the ACS treats it as a new device.
panduan.bind-onu_i3: Leave the save-config (write) option ticked, then click Bind ONU. Without write, the old SN returns when the OLT reboots.
panduan.bind-onu_tip: The server rejects an SN that is not detected on the same port, and every Bind is recorded in the Audit Logs. Refresh the port data before binding.
panduan.aksi-onu_intro: Maintenance actions are available from the per-port ONU page. Availability depends on the OLT vendor/model's capabilities.
panduan.aksi-onu_i0: restart the ONU remotely (the customer drops for about 30–60 seconds).
panduan.aksi-onu_i1: ZTE C300/C320 via SNMP SET (needs the SNMP write community); C-Data and HiOSO HA7304 via CLI; HiOSO HA7302 via SNMP SET (needs the write community). HiOSO ONU names are limited to 32 characters.
panduan.aksi-onu_i2: deactivate an ONU without deleting its registration — the customer is down until it is enabled again (ZTE C300/C320, C-Data, HiOSO).
panduan.aksi-onu_i3: remove the ONU registration from the OLT; the ONU must be registered again. On ZTE, several selected ONUs can be deleted at once.
panduan.aksi-onu_i4: ONU Detail reads status, optics, and the RX trend live over CLI; Configure ONU edits the running-config section by section (view-only on C600).
panduan.aksi-onu_i5: read the source ONU's running-config, then rebuild the registration on the target port (ZTE C300/C320, batch with a progress modal).
panduan.aksi-onu_i6: enable TR069/ACS on every ONU of one PON port at once (ZTE C300/C320) — scan (dry-run) first; ONUs already pointing at the same ACS are skipped.
panduan.aksi-onu_i7: link an ONU to its ODP from the dropdown in the ODP column, and filter the list per ODP — available on the per-port ONU page for every vendor.
panduan.aksi-onu_tip: Reboot, delete, enable/disable, copy ONU, and Bulk TR069 do not save the config automatically — run Save Config if the change must survive an OLT reboot.
panduan.monitoring_intro: The ONU Monitoring menu lists every ONU of one OLT in a single table with full filters, without opening ports one by one. The page is view-only; ONU actions happen on the port page.
panduan.monitoring_i0: Pick an OLT first, then filter by port, state (Online, LOS, Dying Gasp, Offline), admin state, attenuation level, and ODP.
panduan.monitoring_i1: The customer name is each row's primary identity; the Open in port (manage ONU) icon opens the port page with that ONU highlighted.
panduan.monitoring_i2: Scan this OLT's ONUs re-reads every ONU of the OLT over SNMP and updates the per-port cache.
panduan.peta_intro: The ONU Map menu shows customer-ONU pins (green = online, red = offline/LOS/power off) plus ODP pins and their cable lines for every OLT.
panduan.peta_i0: click Add Pin, click the spot on the map, then choose ONU (OLT → port → ONU) or ODP; or use the Add to Map button on the per-port ONU page.
panduan.peta_i1: paste a location link and the coordinates are picked up automatically.
panduan.peta_i2: the pin detail card can rename or reboot the ONU straight from the map, and open the ONU Detail or its port page.
panduan.peta_i3: pins are locked by default. Click Unlock on the detail card to drag one — the new coordinates are saved every time you drop the pin, then click Lock once it sits right.
panduan.odp_intro: The ODP menu groups customer ONUs per field splitter (an ONU belongs to one ODP, an ODP sits on one PON port), then shows each as a pin on the ONU Map with cable lines to its ONUs.
panduan.odp_i0: search ODPs by name, OLT, or PON port; the connected-ONU count shows on every row.
panduan.odp_i1: fill in the name, OLT, PON slot/port (optional), coordinates (manually or by pasting a Google Maps link), and notes. An ODP can move to another OLT/port; ONUs that no longer match are detached after a warning.
panduan.odp_i2: attach or detach ONUs from an ODP through the Manage ONUs modal — an ONU can belong to only one ODP.
panduan.odp_i3: the Colour button colours the ODP pin (palette or Random) and by default applies it to every ODP on the same port; new ODPs on that port inherit it. Green and red are unavailable because they mark ONU status.
panduan.odp_i4: one documentation photo per ODP (JPG/PNG/WebP up to 12 MB, converted to WebP); visible only to signed-in users, and technicians can shoot it straight from the Android app.
panduan.odp_i5: when every ONU behind an ODP goes offline you get a single ODP down alarm; when only some do, their ONU alarms are summarised into one Telegram/push message — not dozens of separate notifications.
panduan.odp_tip: Deleting an ODP is permanent and is not recorded in the Audit Logs — its ONU links go with it (the ONUs on the OLT are unaffected).
panduan.alarm_intro: The Alarms menu is the alarm hub. The system raises alarms only on healthy-to-fault transitions (e.g. ONU online → offline, port up → down, RX out of range).
panduan.alarm_i0: OLT unreachable, PON port down, PON port disabled by admin, ODP down (every ONU of one ODP offline), LOS, power off (dying gasp), ONU offline, and high RX attenuation. Separate LOS and dying gasp are reported only by ZTE and C-Data GPON.
panduan.alarm_i1: Settings → Alarm tab (admin) applies to the main Telegram bot and app push: Realtime or 2-poll confirmation (anti-flap, default), minimum severity, send on raise/clear, alarm types, parent-alarm correlation, and per-ODP summaries.
panduan.alarm_i2: per-OLT (admin/operator) and per-partner alarm switches control who receives notifications — alarm evaluation keeps running.
panduan.alarm_i3: notifications go to the main Telegram bot and Android app push (FCM). A partner's Telegram bot uses its own filters, set under My Telegram Bot.
panduan.alarm_i4: click a notification in the bell (or a row on the Alarms page) to jump to the affected ONU/port/OLT. If the ONU has moved ports, its current position opens; if its old position now belongs to a different customer, the system refuses to open it so you never land on the wrong ONU.
panduan.alarm_tip: The default 2-poll confirmation mode holds an alarm until the fault is seen in two consecutive polls (~10 minutes) so brief flaps don't fire false notifications. Need alerts ASAP? Switch to Realtime in Settings → Alarm.
panduan.telnet_intro: Open a CLI session to the OLT right from the browser (xterm.js terminal window) via the Telnet to OLT icon in the OLT list — no separate telnet app.
panduan.telnet_i0: The window can be dragged, minimized, and maximized.
panduan.telnet_i1: For manual/diagnostic CLI commands on every vendor. Only admins/operators or the partner who owns the OLT, Telnet CLI credentials required, and every session opened is recorded in the Audit Logs.
panduan.report_intro: The Reports menu builds filterable, exportable reports; their content follows your OLT scope.
panduan.report_i0: ONU Inventory & RX Power, OLT Status, Alarm History, and ONU Provisioning.
panduan.report_i1: per OLT, per PON port, time range, status, and RX attenuation status.
panduan.report_i2: download as CSV or PDF via the buttons at the top right.
panduan.pengaturan_intro: The Settings menu (admin only) holds several system configuration tabs.
panduan.pengaturan_i0: app name and logo (white-label), version, system information, and the Download APK button for the Android app.
panduan.pengaturan_i1: the ACS endpoint (URL, username, password) planted on ONUs when registering with TR069 and used by Bulk TR069.
panduan.pengaturan_i2: the central alarm delivery policy for the main Telegram bot and push: Realtime/2-poll confirmation, minimum severity, triggers, alarm types, parent correlation, and per-ODP summaries.
panduan.pengaturan_i3: the main bot's connection: token, chat ID, Send Test, and the bot command webhook. Its alarm filters now live in the Alarm tab.
panduan.pengaturan_i4: the FCM push switch for the Android app, sending a manual notification to every device, and the list of registered devices (revocable).
panduan.pengaturan_i5: issue/revoke REST API tokens for integrations; a token is shown only once when created.
panduan.users_intro: Admins control user access and trace system activity.
panduan.users_i0: add, edit, and delete user accounts; assign each one a role (admin/operator/partner) and its OLT assignment. The list shows each account's role and assigned-OLT count.
panduan.users_i1: an operator without assignments can access every OLT, with assignments only the ticked OLTs; a partner gets only the ticked OLTs plus their own private OLTs. Deleting a partner returns their private OLTs to the shared pool.
panduan.users_i2: a trail of important changes — who changed what and when, including sign-ins, Telnet sessions, Bind ONU, port disable/enable, and VLAN writes. ODP deletions are not recorded.
panduan.partner_intro: Partner accounts see only the OLTs assigned to them and the OLTs they added themselves, and manage their own Telegram bot.
panduan.partner_i0: OLTs a partner adds become private automatically: hidden from admins/operators, with notifications going only to the owner. Only on their own OLTs can a partner change the connection, run Test SNMP, open Telnet, read backup contents, and disable/enable PON ports.
panduan.partner_i1: partners set up their own bot, chat IDs, and alarm filters (minimum severity, triggers, alarm types), independent of the global bot and the admin's Alarm tab.
panduan.mobile_intro: An Android app for technicians, with 5 tabs: Dashboard, OLT, ODP, Map, and Account.
panduan.mobile_i0: the APK must be built with API_BASE_URL pointing at your NMS server (see docs/BUILD_APK.md); an admin can place it on the server so it is offered under Settings → General → Download APK. Sign in with the same email & password as on the web.
panduan.mobile_i1: network summary and search (magnifier icon); OLT → port → ONU → detail to reboot, rename, and delete ONUs; Unconfigured and basic-mode ZTE ONU registration with an optional ODP.
panduan.mobile_i2: list, search, per-OLT filter, and an ODP detail listing its ONUs; the ODP colour and photo (Camera/Gallery/Delete) can be changed straight from the app.
panduan.mobile_i3: a full-screen ONU and ODP map, view-only — adding/moving pins and creating/editing ODPs stay on the web.
panduan.mobile_i4: account info, the Alarms card, a test notification, theme, and Log out. Tap an alarm push to open the related alarm or ONU straight away.
panduan.troubleshooting_i0: check the SNMP IP/port/community and make sure the OLT allows SNMP access from the server.
panduan.troubleshooting_i1: that's the 2-poll confirmation mode (default). For faster alerts, enable Realtime in Settings → Alarm.
panduan.troubleshooting_i2: check that the OLT alarm switch is On, then the Alarm tab in Settings (alarm types & minimum severity) and the Telegram/Mobile connection — use Send Test.
panduan.troubleshooting_i3: your role may lack permission, the account may be in demo mode, or the OLT vendor doesn't support that action.
panduan.troubleshooting_i4s: Changes lost after an OLT reboot
panduan.troubleshooting_i4: the config was not saved — run Save Config after ZTE C300/C320 registrations and other ONU actions.
panduan.troubleshooting_i5: fill in the SNMP write community under Edit OLT (also required for HiOSO HA7302 ONU rename).

users.assign_hint_operator: The operator is limited to the checked OLTs. Leave empty to grant access to all OLTs.
users.assign_hint_partner: The partner can only view & edit the OLTs checked here.
users.no_olt: No OLTs registered yet. Add an OLT first.
users.password_new: New Password (leave blank to keep the current one)
users.delete_msg: Delete user "{name}" ({email})? This action is permanent.

auditlogs.list_sub: A record of user actions & data changes in the system.
auditlogs.empty_filtered: No audit logs match the filter.

profile.title: Profile
profile.info_sub: Update your account's profile information and email address.
profile.name: Name
profile.resend: Click here to re-send the verification email.
profile.verification_sent: A new verification link has been sent to your email address.
profile.password_sub: Ensure your account is using a long, random password to stay secure.
profile.delete_sub: Once your account is deleted, all of its resources and data will be permanently deleted. Before deleting your account, please download any data or information that you wish to retain.
profile.delete_confirm_title: Are you sure you want to delete your account?
profile.delete_confirm_sub: Once your account is deleted, all of its resources and data will be permanently deleted. Please enter your password to confirm you would like to permanently delete your account.

telegrambot.scope_before: This bot only receives alarms & serves commands for the
telegrambot.scope_after: assigned to your account by the admin.
telegrambot.section_sub_partner: Send your OLT/ONU alarms to your own Telegram bot or group.
telegrambot.enable_hint: When off, alarms are still stored but not sent to Telegram.
telegrambot.token_saved_placeholder: •••••••• (token saved — leave blank to keep it)
telegrambot.token_hint: Get a token from @BotFather on Telegram via the /newbot command.
telegrambot.chat_id_placeholder: e.g. 123456789 or -1001234567890. Separate multiple IDs with commas.
telegrambot.chat_id_hint: For personal chats: message the bot then check @userinfobot. For groups: add the bot to the group; group IDs start with a minus sign.
telegrambot.min_severity_hint: Only alarms at this severity or higher are sent.
telegrambot.on_raise: Send when a new alarm is raised
telegrambot.on_raise_hint: Notify when a new alarm triggers during a polling cycle.
telegrambot.on_clear_hint: Notify when an active alarm returns to normal.
telegrambot.types_hint: Only the checked alarm types are sent to Telegram.
telegrambot.types_none: Nothing checked — all alarm notifications are off.
telegrambot.webhook_sub_partner: The bot replies to commands from registered chat IDs (read-only, your OLTs only).
telegrambot.commands_hint: When enabled & the webhook is registered, the bot answers /status, /olt, /alarm, /onu.
telegrambot.webhook_need_token: Save the bot token first before registering the webhook.
telegrambot.need_token_chat: Save the token & chat ID first to send a test.
telegrambot.section_sub_admin: Send the latest OLT/ONU alarms to a Telegram bot or group.
telegrambot.webhook_sub_admin: The bot replies to commands from registered chat IDs (read-only).
telegrambot.commands_hint_admin: When enabled & the webhook is registered, the bot answers /status, /olt, /alarm, /onu, /prov.
telegrambot.types_hint_admin: Only the checked alarm types are sent to Telegram. E.g. check only LOS, Power Off, High RX attenuation, and GPON port down.

settings.title: Settings
settings.identity_sub: The name, version, and logo shown across the app.
settings.logo_hint: PNG, JPG, or WEBP. Max 1 MB. Leave empty to use the default logo.
settings.app_version_hint: Shown on the system panel in the sidebar.
settings.android_sub: Download & install the KusumaVision NMS mobile app.
settings.apk_missing_hint: Build it on the server first with bash bin/build-apk.sh; the result is copied automatically to public/downloads/.
settings.acs_sub: Used by the "Bulk TR069" feature on the per-port ONU page (ZTE OLTs).
settings.acs_url_hint: Full ACS server address including the port, e.g. http://acs.example.net:7547.
settings.acs_pw_hint: Leave blank to keep the old password.
settings.acs_note: The bulk TR069 scan marks an ONU as already active only when its TR069 is unlocked and its URL + username exactly match the values above. ONUs that are inactive or point to a different ACS are rewritten with this URL, username, and password.
settings.alarm_sub: One place for every alarm rule: when they are sent, which ones are sent, and how large outages are summarised. Applies to Telegram & the mobile app.
settings.alarm_central_note: Every alarm filter now lives on this page. The Telegram Bot & Mobile Notifications tabs only handle their connection (token/chat id, push switch, device list).
settings.alarm_suppress_children: Send only the parent alarm when a PON port / ODP is down
settings.alarm_suppress_children_hint: On: when a PON port goes down, only that port's alarm is sent — none of the ONUs under it. Same when every ONU in one ODP is down: a single "ODP down" alarm. The ONU alarms are still recorded on the Alarms page, they are just not notified (recovery included).
settings.alarm_group_odp: Summarise several ONUs of one ODP into a single message
settings.alarm_group_odp_hint: When only part of an ODP is down, send one message listing the customers instead of one message per customer.
settings.alarm_types_hint: Only the checked types are sent to Telegram & the mobile app. Every type is still recorded on the Alarms page.
settings.alarm_filter_moved: Alarm filters (minimum severity, triggers, alarm types) are now centralised on the Alarm tab — click here to open it.
settings.alarm_toggle_hint: On: the fault must still be present at the next check (2× polls, ~10 minutes) before a notification is sent — damping false alarms from brief flaps. Off: realtime, notifications go out as soon as the fault is first detected.
settings.alarm_note: This setting applies globally to every OLT and every channel (Telegram + mobile), and takes effect on the next poll without a restart. Alarms are always recorded in the history; this only controls the notification timing. Realtime is faster but may notify about momentary faults that recover immediately.
settings.fcm_sub: Push switch for the Android app via Firebase (FCM). Which alarms get sent is set on the Alarm tab.
settings.fcm_creds: Firebase credentials are not installed on the server yet (service-account JSON + FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS). Pushes won't be sent until that is set up.
settings.fcm_enable_hint: When off, alarms are still stored but not sent to the mobile app.
settings.fcm_on_raise_hint: Push when a new alarm triggers.
settings.fcm_on_clear_hint: Push when an alarm returns to normal.
settings.fcm_types_hint: Only the checked alarm types are sent.
settings.fcm_types_none: Nothing checked — all alarm pushes are off.
settings.fcm_manual_sub: Broadcast a message to every registered mobile app ({n} devices).
settings.fcm_body_placeholder: Write the message that will appear in the phone notification…
settings.fcm_no_devices: No devices registered yet (users must log in on the app first).
settings.api_disabled_note: All /api endpoints are turned off for security (zero attack surface) since no app uses them yet. Tokens can still be prepared, but only work after the API is enabled on the server: set $apiEnabled = true in routes/api.php then reload PHP-FPM.
settings.api_access_sub: Tokens for calling NMS data from another web app or Android.
settings.api_base_hint: Token-protected endpoints, e.g. {url}/onus. Send the header Authorization: Bearer <token>.
settings.api_public_hint: Aggregate numbers without customer data — safe for widgets on other sites. Full documentation: docs/API.md.
settings.api_new_token_title: New token created — copy it now
settings.api_new_token_note: For security, the token is only shown once. Store it somewhere safe (e.g. the other app's server .env).
settings.api_personal_sub: Each token grants access as your account. Revoke it any time.
settings.token_name_placeholder: e.g. Billing Web, Technician Android App
settings.api_enable_first: Enable the API on the server first before creating tokens.
settings.tokens_empty: No tokens yet. Create one above to start using the API from another app.
settings.token_warning: Tokens are secrets, like passwords. Don't put them in code visible to the public/browser. For other websites, store them server-side (e.g. .env) and call the API from the server.
settings.revoke_confirm: Revoke this token? Apps using it will lose access immediately.
settings.devices_sub: Every phone logged into the mobile app (all users). Revoke a token to cut off a lost/unused phone.
settings.devices_empty: No devices have logged into the app yet.
settings.devices_revoke_confirm: Revoke this device token? The app on that phone loses access immediately and must log in again.
settings.devices_fcm_sub: Devices receiving push notifications. Delete to stop push to a specific phone (separate from login tokens).
settings.devices_fcm_delete_confirm: Delete this device push registration? That phone stops receiving notifications until it logs in again.

welcome.hero_desc: Monitor, provision, and manage ZTE C300/C320/C600 OLTs — now multi-vendor with C-Data & HiOSO — from one place, complete with an ONU location map and an Android app. Built for Indonesian ISP operations that demand speed and accuracy.
welcome.hw_desc: Mature SNMP & CLI drivers for ZTE C300, C320, and C600 — now extended to C-Data EPON (17409) & GPON (34592) plus HiOSO EPON (25355) OLTs. Battle-tested on Indonesian ISPs' production OLTs.
welcome.features_title: Everything You Need in One Platform
welcome.features_sub: Purpose-built for Indonesian ISP FTTH/GPON operations — from monitoring to remote management.
welcome.f_multivendor_body: Manage ZTE, C-Data (EPON & GPON), and HiOSO EPON OLTs side by side in one dashboard — cross-OLT ONU monitoring, plus rename, reboot & delete ONUs right from the dashboard.
welcome.f_map_body: Map your customer/ONU spread across OLTs on an interactive map — add pins from a map click or a Google Maps link, lock/unlock a pin then drag it to fix its position, plus ONU reboot & rename right from the customer's location.
welcome.f_android_body: An Android mobile app to watch OLTs & ONUs, register, reboot/rename, and receive real-time alarm push notifications via Firebase — the NOC stays connected anywhere.
welcome.f_inventory_body: Manage every OLT device, card, and GPON port in one centralized inventory with capability detection — including PON port description editing straight from the dashboard via CLI.
welcome.f_odp_body: ODP (splitter) pins on the map with animated ODP→ONU cable lines that follow customer status, plus a dedicated ODP page: CRUD, filters per OLT & PON port, and a Manage ONUs modal. An ODP column and filter sit in every vendor's ONU table, and an ODP can be picked right at ONU registration.
welcome.f_backup_body: Daily scheduled or manual OLT running-config backups — encrypted version history, automatic dedup, diff between versions, view & download. Plus a save-config-to-OLT-memory button for every vendor.
welcome.f_api_body: Integrate the NMS with your systems via a token-based REST API — read summary, OLTs, ONUs, alarms, plus ONU registration & actions (reboot/rename/delete) across vendors.
welcome.f_monitoring_body: Watch every ONU across OLTs & ports on one page — customer name as the primary identity, online/LOS/power-loss status, RX optical power, with quick filters per OLT, port, status, and ODP.
welcome.f_provisioning_body: Generate ZTE provisioning CLI scripts — C300/C320 & now C600 (Model B/SmartOLT TR-069, auto mgmt-IP) — register, T-CONT, VLAN, PPPoE/DHCP/Static/Bridge, executed via Telnet; plus per-port bulk TR-069 & ONU config copy between ports.
welcome.f_polling_body: Scheduled polling for system info, port status, and the ONU table — all stored as per-OLT snapshots.
welcome.f_alarm_body: Raise/clear alarms with Critical/Major/Minor/Warning severities, two-poll anti-flap confirmation, and root-cause correlation (a port-down holds back the ONU alarm storm). Click a notification to open the affected ONU/port/OLT.
welcome.f_remote_body: Reboot, rename, enable/disable, delete ONUs, and open/close the ONT web UI remotely (Remote ONT) — all from the dashboard, no SSH into the OLT.
welcome.f_telnet_body: Access the OLT CLI right from the browser via an xterm.js terminal — draggable window, minimize/maximize, auto-login, no separate telnet app.
welcome.f_search_body: Find an OLT or ONU instantly by serial number, customer name, or interface — and jump straight to its port.
welcome.f_reports_body: Network statistics reports — port utilization, RX optical power (warning/critical), and OLT status — downloadable per OLT or time range.
welcome.f_notif_body: Important alarms go to Telegram groups/chats & Android push notifications — ONUs going down behind one ODP arrive as a single message instead of dozens. Plus an interactive bot (button menus): check OLT & ONU status, find customers, even refresh an OLT from anywhere.
welcome.f_audit_body: An indelible audit trail for every configuration change, login, and telnet access — complete with actor, time, and old→new diff.
welcome.f_rbac_body: Separate access for admins, NOC operators, and partners — partners only see & manage their own private OLTs; sensitive features like audit logs & system settings stay admin-only.
welcome.how_title: From Device to Operations in 4 Steps
welcome.how_sub: The same workflow the NOC team uses every day — connected, monitored, and provisioned without hopping between tools.
welcome.step1_body: Register ZTE OLTs (IP, SNMP community, CLI credentials) into a centralized inventory with automatic capability detection.
welcome.step2_body: A Go engine polls system info, GPON port status, and the ONU table on schedule — stored as per-OLT snapshots.
welcome.step3_body: Generate ZTE CLI scripts (register, T-CONT, VLAN, PPPoE/DHCP/Static, TR-069) then execute them directly via Telnet from the browser.
welcome.step4_body: Watch RX power & ONU status, receive important alarms via Telegram, then download utilization & optical reports per time range.
welcome.gallery_sub: From the dashboard to ONU provisioning — a clean interface designed for NOC operational speed.

welcome.modules_sub: Every module is designed to be lean, with a workflow that feels natural to the NOC team.
